steps.title: Open Tapeology
steps.narration: We start on Tapeology's home screen, which opens in Simulated mode by default. The main area sits quietly idle, waiting for you to pick a ticker to watch.
steps.point_out: The Live / Historical / Simulated switch and the ticker box across the top, with "No ticker watched" filling the main area.

steps.title: Switch to Historical data
steps.narration: One click on "Historical" turns Tapeology into a time machine — the controls for replaying a real past trading session appear right here on the same screen, no extra page to find.
steps.point_out: A symbol search box plus Date, Start time, End time, and a replay-speed picker, all revealed in place.

steps.title: Search for a real symbol
steps.narration: Start typing part of a symbol and Tapeology suggests real, tradable matches — the ticker on the left, the company name on the right.
steps.point_out: The live dropdown under the box: real matches such as AAPL · Apple Inc. appear as you type "AAP".

steps.title: Pick a suggestion
steps.narration: Click any match and it drops straight into the symbol box — or you can ignore the list entirely and just type the symbol yourself.
steps.point_out: The symbol box now holds the symbol you picked from the list.

steps.title: Type the ticker to replay
steps.narration: Here we just type Ford's ticker, F, by hand — free-text entry always works, with or without the dropdown.
steps.point_out: F sitting in the symbol box, ready to replay.

steps.title: Choose the past date
steps.narration: Pick the calendar date of the session you want to relive.
steps.point_out: The date set to a recent trading day.

steps.title: Set the start time
steps.narration: Set the start of the window you want to watch.
steps.point_out: Start time entered for the replay window.

steps.title: Set the end time
steps.narration: And the end of the window — here a tight two-minute slice of the tape.
steps.point_out: End time entered, defining the full replay window.

steps.title: Pick a replay speed
steps.narration: Choose how fast to replay — 10× compresses a couple of minutes of real tape into a few seconds.

steps.title: Replay real Ford order flow
steps.narration: Press Watch and the full cockpit fills with Ford's real trades and quotes for that window — read exactly the same way Tapeology reads a simulated tape.
steps.point_out: Real bid/ask/spread/last, real recent trades, the live tape state "Bid Absorption" with its confidence, and the "historical F …" label up top — all from genuine market data.

steps.title: Try a symbol that isn't real
steps.narration: Now we deliberately ask for a symbol that doesn't exist as a tradable stock.
steps.point_out: A made-up symbol typed into the box.

steps.title: Honest answer: not tradable
steps.narration: Instead of inventing numbers, Tapeology says plainly that this isn't a tradable symbol — and shows no cockpit at all.
steps.point_out: An amber panel reading "Symbol not tradable" with the phrase "not a tradable symbol" — and no fabricated tape anywhere.

steps.title: Back to a real symbol
steps.narration: Back to Ford — but this time we'll point it at a window when the market was closed.
steps.point_out: F typed into the box again.

steps.title: Pick a closed-market day
steps.narration: We choose a weekend date, when no trading happened at all.
steps.point_out: The date set to a market-closed day.

steps.title: Honest answer: no data
steps.narration: Again Tapeology refuses to guess: with no trades in that window it simply says so, rather than drawing a fake tape.
steps.point_out: An amber "No data for that window" panel standing in place of the cockpit.

steps.title: Back to Simulated mode
steps.narration: Switching back to Simulated confirms the built-in scenarios still work exactly as they always did.
steps.point_out: The plain ticker box returns and the historical date/time controls tuck away.

steps.title: Watch a built-in scenario
steps.narration: We type one of the built-in scenarios, SIM-BUYER, and press Watch.
steps.point_out: SIM-BUYER entered in the plain ticker box.

steps.title: Simulated tape still reads true
steps.narration: The simulated tape plays through the very same cockpit and is correctly read as buyers in control — proving the new real-data work didn't change how the built-in scenarios behave.
steps.point_out: The cockpit reaching "Buyer Control" with its confidence, just as it did before this iteration.

steps.title: Stop watching
steps.narration: Press Stop and the cockpit clears cleanly back to the calm idle screen, ready for the next ticker.
steps.point_out: Back to "No ticker watched" with no leftover data lingering on screen.
